title: Pumpkin and Snow Pea Laksa
subtitle: with Coriander and Roasted Peanuts
description: What's better than a warming bowl of laksa on a winter's night? This one is sweetened with roasted pumpkin, dotted with crisp snow peas and topped off with crunchy peanuts. It's oh so slurpable!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Trim the stems from the snow peas, removing the strings from one side, then halve lengthwise on an angle. Pick the coriander leaves and finely chop the stems. Halve the unpeeled pumpkin widthwise, then cut into 4 wedges. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves.

Roast pumpkin: Put the pumpkin on the lined tray and drizzle with 2 tsp vegetable oil. Season with salt and pepper and turn to coat. Roast, turning halfway, for 20 mins or until tender. Put 2 pumpkin wedges in a bowl and mash the flesh, discarding the skins. Meanwhile, bring a small saucepan of water to the boil for the eggs.

Cook laksa: Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook the coriander stems, garlic and 2 tbs laksa spice blend (see Make it yours), stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant. Add the coconut milk, mashed pumpkin, 1 tbs soy sauce, ½ tsp white vinegar and 500ml (2 cups) water and bring to the boil.

Boil eggs: Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6 mins or until slightly thickened. Add the snow peas and cook for 2 mins or until just tender. Remove the pan from the heat. Meanwhile, cook 2 eggs in the pan of boiling water for 6 mins for soft-boiled or 8 mins for hard-boiled. Remove from the pan and cool in cold water. Peel and halve the eggs.

Serve up: Put three-quarters of the noodles in a large heatproof bowl, cover generously with boiling water and soak for 2 mins, using a fork to gently separate the noodles after they start to soften. Drain. Divide the noodles among bowls and spoon over the laksa. Top with the pumpkin wedges, eggs, coriander leaves and peanuts. Enjoy!

Make it yours: Our laksa spice blend is mild, but it does have some warmth. If serving this to young ones, reduce the amount to taste. Depending on your palate, you may want to add a pinch of sugar to the laksa to help balance out the acidity of the vinegar.
